recipes.name: Texas Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can crushed pineapple with juice

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).

Pour cherry pie filling into a 9x13-inch baking dish; top with pineapple but do not stir. Sprinkle cake mix over pineapple; sprinkle coconut over cake mix. Sprinkle pecans over coconut; pour melted margarine over top.
Bake in the preheated oven until top is golden brown, about 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Texas Pie
raw_recipe.description: This quick-to-make, big as Texas pie recipe features cherry pie filling, crushed pineapple, coconut, and pecans, all baked with a butter cake mix.

review.reviewBody: I added almond extract into the cherry pie filling and sprinkled 1/2 cup brown sugar over the fruit. I followed the advice of Mommaward and mixed the melted butter into the cake mix. I only used 3/4 cup butter, sprinkled about 1/2 cup pecans over all, did not add coconut. It was delicious. Nice crunch on top, cobbler-ish in the bottom. I will try it with peach pie filling. Great recipe!
I made it with butter instead of margarine .

I'll start by saying I made a couple of tweaks to this recipe. I used a 9"x 9" non-stick baking pan I found at Walmart. No spray needed. Poured in one can cherry filling, one can of crushed pineapple, one Dolly Parton Coconut flavored cake mix (also found at Walmart Market). I did not measure my coconut flakes but generously added what looked like a good amount to me. Then I sprinkled a couple of handfuls of slivered almonds on that and placed one stick of butter in the microwave to melt. Drizzled the melted butter on top of this recipe and the pan was filled to nearly the brim. I was concerned it might spill over while baking but it didn't at all. I Cooked it for exactly 40 minutes until it was slightly browned and placed it on a cooling rack for one hour. So pretty! It was still warm when I sliced into it after dinner. I served it up to my husband with a heaping scoop of Carb Smart Vanilla ice cream. This recipe was so sloppi-liciously killer-good when warm and had a bit of crunch to it as well which I love. I will make this one again and again. Great recipe LTEDFORD, my hubby and I thank you for sharing it!

Easy and tasty. You can see it's almost gone. It keeps well under a cloth on the counter. I had a slightly smaller dish, so reduced the ingredient amounts. Even so, baked it for an extra 25 mins. Lined the dish with Filo dough to give it a solid bottom. Used only 1 smaller can of my fave raspberry filling, not a big can of cherry filling. I used 2/3 a 15.6oz package of cake mix. Also added mini chocolate chips, however I would not necessarily recommend that because it clashes a little with the fruit. I used vegan butter and it worked great. Also sprinkled brown sugar on top to candy the pecans, my favorite. The pineapple cake mush baked great, and the toasted coconut gave it more excellent texture. If I make this again, I might layer filo dough between the flavors and/or split the cake-pineapple mixture a little between each layer to give it a more attractive cross-section.

Made this. We followed the recipe exactly Even adding additional cake mix as mixes on shelves are 3.25 oz short of what is called for. I would add additional cherry pie filling and pineapple filling as they barely covered the bottom of the baking dish. I would cut back on the coconut as the coconut overwhelmed the other flavors OR don't use sweetened coconut as there is enough sweetness in the pie filling and pineapple. Next, being a pecan lover, I would add an additional 1/2 cup of pecans.

I’m gluten intolerant so I used a gluten-free cake mix, and I used canned unsweetened cherries instead of cherry pie filling, and of course I used butter instead of margarine. Also used unsweetened coconut. I think it would have been too sweet without those tweaks. But it turned out perfectly and was delicious. I’m making it again for a holiday pot luck party tonight. 😊

I make this all the time but know it as dump cake. I omit the coconut as my family doesn't like it. I put the pecans in with the fruit, it softens them a bit but still has texture. Any yellow or white cake mix works. I've also made with apple pie filling. Yummy every time!

This is so quick and easy! It was a recipe in my book for a hotel and restaurant management class that I took in college as a fun elective. This was 50 years ago! While Texas may lay claim to it, now, I still have that recipe spiral from college, lol. There are so many variations. You can use a spice cake with peach or apple pie filling, strawberry cake mix with strawberry pie filling, etc. White cake mixes work well with this, as well. Don’t be afraid to try all different cake mixes and pie fillings, and you can add all kinds of toppings, fillings, etc! It is almost impossible to have a bad turnout, lol. it is so quick and simple, and I have been making different versions of this for fifty years. My family still requests it when they visit! It’s the only reason I have boxed cake mixes in my pantry, as cakes are easy to bake from scratch.

My family loves this dessert. It’s a favorite of everyone, however, I have to make two when we have family picnics or big get togethers. One I make just exactly like this recipe here, yummy! The other I leave out the nuts and coconut because picky eaters, and not the children! I love it because it’s delicious and so easy to make. And I call that a win/win!
For an even fancier presentation try making it in a springform pan and putting it in a glass triffle bowl the same size as the springform pan
this pie was delicious. I used a gluten-free yellow cake mix instead of the regular cake mix. Next time I will have apple pie filling. I am allergic to wheat.

I followed the recipe to the letter. I was very excited for it to be done. When removed from the oven it seemed to be really runny. I put it back in the oven for another 10 minutes. It still did not get as brown on top as I thought that it should. I put it out to set for 10 more minutes. When it was finally cook enough to eat it - it turned out good. We had it with some cool whip on top.

You had me drooling right up to where I saw 'margarine' in your recipe. Anyone that would use this in their ingredients is immediately suspect to me. However, I tried this with real butter and it was quite good.

I did like it and my coworkers as well. It was a little on the sweet side for me but I'm sure a scoop of vanilla ice cream would have made a difference. I substituted blueberry pie filling for the cherry and did 2 cans verses the one. I also only had a white box cake and used that and it was fine. Even people that dont typically like coconut loved it. It may be a dump cake but what does a name matter. If it's recieved with compliments and devoured, c'est la vie.

Yes, it is a dump cake for those of you who only commented on this recipe with an attitude. And just like poke cakes there are a hundred different varieties you can use for ingredients, but this combination I think is "special"( for those of you who complained that there is nothing special about this cake), I made it, I loved it, my family loves it, so when u can make a simple dessert that brings the whole family together and make everyone happy and smile...THAT IS SOMETHING SPECIAL! Thank you very much!
This is a dump cake, regardless of the newfangled name.
It’s just a different name for what’s been called a “Dump Cake” forever, nothing special about it
Delicious. I did not change a thing!!
